sentences.text: The genus Archaeoistiodactylus is known from an incomplete skeleton that preserves a partial skull and lower jaws. The metacarpal bones in the hand of this animal are notably short.
Archaeoistiodactylus holds the distinction of being the oldest known istiodactylid pterosaur.
The genus was first named and described by Lü Junchang and Fucha Xiaohui in 2010.
Phylogenetic analyses later showed Archaeoistiodactylus falling in a polytomy with wukongopterids, supporting its affinity with that clade.
A 2021 study considered Archaeoistiodactylus to be an undiagnostic wukongopterid.

Fossils of Archaeoistiodactylus were recovered from the Tiaojishan Formation in western Liaoning, China, dating to the Bathonian and Callovian stages of the Jurassic. The holotype fossil dates to the Middle Jurassic, between the Bathonian and Callovian stages, approximately 165 million years ago.
